title: Do Calorie‑Restricted Diets Work? - Nautilus
gist: Calorie-restricted diets — intermittent fasting, alternate-day fasting and the Fast 800 — have drawn heavy interest for weight loss, resting on the simple premise that eating less should cut weight, with the open question being whether the weight is regained.

insights.claim: In the last few years there has been a lot of interest in calorie-restricted diets for weight loss.
insights.speaker: Olivia Wills
insights.so_what: Sustained consumer demand for diet programs is a tailwind for weight-loss services and products.

insights.claim: Calorie-restricted diets range from intermittent fasting (eating within a set daily window) and alternate-day fasting (limited or no calories every other day) to the Fast 800, which drives rapid weight loss through drastic calorie cuts combined with a Mediterranean diet.
insights.speaker: Olivia Wills
insights.so_what: Maps the competitive landscape of diet approaches.

insights.claim: The basic premise of calorie restriction is that eating less should theoretically produce weight loss, but the article questions whether such diets work long term or just lead to weight regain.
insights.speaker: Olivia Wills
insights.so_what: Weight regain risk is a key debate for the durability of diet-based versus pharmacological weight-loss approaches.
